question.explanation:
The formula for ${}_nP_r$ is given by

\[ {}_nP_r = \dfrac {n!} {(n - r)!} \,. \]

$P(5,2)$ means the same thing as $_{5}P_2.$ Using the usual formula for ${}_nP_r,$ we get

\[ \require{cancel} \eqalign{P(5,2) &= \dfrac{5!}{(5-2)!} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{5!}{3!} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{5 \cdot 4 \cdot \cancel{ 3!}}{\cancel{ 3!}} \\[5pt] &= 5 \cdot 4 \\[5pt] &= 20. } \]

example.title: Calculating a Permutation Given Using Alternate Notation

question.text: There are $11$ people taking an online quiz at the same time. How many ways can people finish in first, second, and third place, assuming there are no ties?
question.explanation:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula \[ _{n}P_r = \frac{n!}{(n-r)!}. \]

There are $11$ people, so $n=11.$ We want to select $3$ of those people to come first, second, or third, so we have $r=3.$

Therefore, the number of different ways to place the people is

\[ \eqalign{ \require{cancel} _{11}P_{3} &= \dfrac{11!}{(11-3)!} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{11!}{8!} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{11\cdot 10 \cdot 9 \cdot \cancel{8!}}{\cancel{8!}} \\[5pt] &= 11 \cdot 10 \cdot 9 \\[5pt] &= 990. } \]

example.title: Calculating the Number of Permutations of Objects Chosen From a Group of at Least Ten

question.text: The $8$ members of a club are asked to elect $4$ officials: a president, a vice-president, a secretary, and a treasurer. How many different ways of electing the officials are possible?
question.explanation:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

\[ _{n}P_r = \frac{n!}{(n-r)!}. \]

There are $8$ members to choose from, so $n=8.$ We want to select $4$ of those members to be officials, so we have $r=4.$

Therefore, the number of different $4$-member official teams is

\[ \require{cancel} \eqalign{ {}_8P_4 &= \dfrac {8!} {(8 - 4)!} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {8!} {4!} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {8 \cdot 7 \cdot 6 \cdot 5 \cdot \cancel{4!}} {\cancel{4!}} \\[5pt] &= 8 \cdot 7 \cdot 6 \cdot 5 \\[5pt] &= 1\,680. } \]

example.title: Calculating the Number of Permutations of Objects Chosen From a Group Fewer Than Ten

question.text: Ashley has $5$ tasks. She decides to do one on Thursday and another on Friday. How many different choices of the two tasks does Ashley have?
question.explanation:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula \[ _{n}P_r = \frac{n!}{(n-r)!}. \]

There are $5$ tasks to choose from, so $n=5.$ We want to select $2$ of those for Ashley to do, so we have $r=2.$

Therefore, the number of different choices is

\[ \require{cancel} \eqalign{ {}_5P_2 &= \dfrac {5!} {(5 - 2)!} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {5!} {3!} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac {5\cdot 4\cdot \cancel{3!}} {\cancel{3!}} \\[5pt] &= 5\cdot 4 \\[5pt] &= 20. } \]

example.title: Calculating the Number of Permutations of Objects Chosen From a Group Fewer Than Ten

question.text: Erika has a crayon box with $36$ different colors. She wants to draw each side of a square with a different color. How many possible choices of colors does Erika have?
question.explanation:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula \[ _{n}P_r = \frac{n!}{(n-r)!}. \]

There are $36$ colors to choose from, so $n=36.$ We want to select $4$ of those colors to draw the sides of the square, so we have $r=4.$

Therefore, the number of possible choices is

\[ \eqalign{ \require{cancel} _{36}P_{4} &= \dfrac{36!}{(36-4)!} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{36!}{32!} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{36\cdot 35 \cdot 34 \cdot 33\cdot \cancel{32!}}{\cancel{32!}} \\[5pt] &= 36\cdot 35 \cdot 34 \cdot 33 \\[5pt] &= 1\,413\,720. } \]
